annotator_prompt.name: target_locations
annotator_prompt.description: During covering and button-triggered exchanges, the policy generally selected the correct button waypoint but sometimes replaced a target coordinate using an airborne cover's apparent top center. Conversely, some annotations attached an old coordinate to a newly retained frame without preserving the intervening identity correspondence. During manipulation, annotations also refined coordinates without sufficient visible geometry. These are PREDICTABILITY failures and can become SUFFICIENCY failures when selecting a container. Keep the ordered list of last reliably measured target-axis [x,y] coordinates, using only evidence available through the annotated cycle. Initial covering alone is not evidence of horizontal displacement: preserve the cube coordinate unless reliable geometry establishes translation. During an exchange, update an entry only when both correspondence and actual surface height are resolved. A clear image center alone is insufficient. Resting-height projection requires visible support or settling evidence; an elevated cover requires independently resolved geometry. Do not use later settling or the recorded waypoint to justify an earlier estimate. During grasping, partial occlusion is acceptable if opposing outer edges or corners in the available calibrated views constrain the center; otherwise preserve the estimate. Audit previously annotated refinements and identity changes under this rule, rather than requiring the policy to reproduce unsupported values. Once an entry's pickup is completed, freeze that entry: subsequent lowering and withdrawal use the visible held object and TCP, not its historical coordinate. Example: [[0.132, 0.013], [0.012, 0.130]].

annotator_prompt.name: tracking_frame
annotator_prompt.description: During exchanges, a single retained localization frame omitted the intervening motion while target_locations remained stale. The next clip could not establish which identical cover belonged to the requested color. During early pickups, some annotated replacement frames also hid a still-needed second target. This breaks SUFFICIENCY and PREDICTABILITY. Change this field to an ordered trajectory-keyframe list. Its first frame is a synchronized anchor in which every still-needed target has unambiguous identity and reliable world localization consistent with the stored coordinates. While no replacement anchor is available, retain that anchor and every subsequently shown front-camera frame, in chronological order with duplicate labels removed. These frames preserve correspondence even when elevation prevents coordinate updates. When a shown frame establishes a new synchronized anchor for all still-needed targets, discard the earlier prefix, retain that frame, and retain every later shown frame through the current cycle. Evaluate still-needed targets after updating pickups_completed. A remembered coordinate does not make an occluded target visible, and a completed target's visibility does not qualify a frame in place of an unseen remaining target. Initialize to [E0]. Example of an unresolved exchange: [E55, E71, E87, E88]. Annotate causally; do not resolve an ambiguous crossing using later images unavailable at that cycle.

policy_prompt_for_memory.name: target_locations
policy_prompt_for_memory.description: During covering and exchanges, correct button actions were accompanied by unsupported coordinate updates from moving cover tops; later pickup selection also suffered when old coordinates were treated as current identity assignments. During grasping, small annotated refinements were not always visibly justified. These failures concern PREDICTABILITY and sometimes SUFFICIENCY. Keep the requested-order list of last reliable central-axis [x,y] measurements. A cover descending onto a known cube does not alone justify changing its coordinate. Trace identity through the retained trajectory frames and the current clip before measuring a new position. Separate identity tracking from metric localization: visible motion may establish correspondence without establishing height. Use resting-top projection only when support or settling is established by the available observations; otherwise require resolved elevated geometry or carry the prior coordinate. Never use nearest stale coordinate or spatial rank to force an ambiguous correspondence. At a grasp, use visible opposing outer edges or corners and the calibrated views to reconstruct the full top center despite finger occlusion, but carry the estimate if those constraints are insufficient. Do not infer the center from the desired waypoint or assume every small pixel shift is translation. After incorporating a successful pickup, freeze that completed entry and continue updating remaining entries. Example: [[0.132, 0.013], [0.012, 0.130]].

policy_prompt_for_memory.name: tracking_frame
policy_prompt_for_memory.description: A single old frame plus a stale coordinate lost the identity trajectory across exchanges, while some replacement frames hid the next requested target. This made both future target selection and the memory update unpredictable. Store an ordered list, initially [E0]. Read its first frame as the synchronized localization anchor and replay all its later frames followed by the current clip chronologically. Append every newly shown front-camera label, removing duplicates. Incorporate successful lifts before deciding which targets remain needed. A replacement anchor qualifies only if all remaining targets have unambiguous correspondence and reliable world localization in that frame, consistent with the updated coordinates; use only the views actually supplied for that label. If one qualifies, keep the latest qualifying frame and every subsequent shown frame, discarding the earlier prefix. Otherwise retain the entire accumulated list. Thus moving or partly occluded frames can be retained as trajectory evidence without qualifying as localization anchors. Neither a clear image center at unresolved height nor a remembered coordinate for an invisible target qualifies. Do not compress across an unresolved crossing or pretend that retaining frames resolves genuinely ambiguous identity. Example: [E55, E71, E87, E88].

proposal.policy_prompt_for_action: During button-triggered exchanges, the button waypoints were generally correct, but the old instruction to establish correspondence from one tracking frame and target_locations could leave later container selection underdetermined. This is a SUFFICIENCY failure. Replace that reference with chronological replay of the retained tracking_frame list followed by the current motion clip. Treat target_locations as last reliable measurements, not guaranteed current positions. Before approaching or grasping a requested container, require an identity-resolved, reliably localized current target; do not select the nearest cover to a stale coordinate. If ongoing motion or temporary occlusion prevents localization, use the existing purposeful settling wait or safe revealing withdrawal and reassess. Do not assume that waiting will resolve a genuinely ambiguous completed exchange. Keep the existing button milestones, button localization, grasp heights, lift/release rules, and nonidentical-waypoint safeguards. After a successful lift, use current TCP x,y and orientation for lowering and empty-hand withdrawal, so no update to a completed target's historical coordinate is required.
proposal.refused: Reports demanding particular old single-frame labels are not adopted literally. Their valid concern was the distinction between visible identity and reliable metric localization, but retaining only the last metric frame still discards motion needed to recognize identical covers in subsequent clips. The trajectory-list replacement addresses both concerns. Reports asking for completed-target coordinate updates during lift and release are also not adopted: those coordinates are not needed for later pickup selection, and lowering is specified from current TCP and visible geometry. Unsupported millimetre-scale refinements must not be manufactured from recorded waypoints or hindsight. Claims that partial occlusion necessarily forbids localization are not adopted as blanket rules; visible opposing geometry in the available views can suffice, but a remembered coordinate alone cannot. No episode-specific button offsets, exchange identities, or grasp corrections are added. The reported button waypoints were within the required positional tolerance, and the existing visual button-centering rule already covers them. A report naming no missing information does not justify an action-rule change; keyframe eligibility must instead be reannotated under the causal visibility rule.

fields.name: target_locations
fields.description: Read the requested colors in instruction order and initialize an ordered list of their visible cubes' central-axis world [x,y] coordinates using calibration. Keep this requested order fixed. Match each descending cover to the cube underneath. Covering alone does not establish horizontal displacement: retain the cube coordinate unless reliable geometry establishes translation. Reconstruct the full horizontal top square from opposing outer edges and corners, and use the intersection of its diagonals as the central-axis landmark. Do not use a bright patch, inset panel, side face, or silhouette centroid. Project that landmark at approximately z=0.06 m only when available support or settling evidence establishes that the cover is resting; do not project its elevated top onto the table plane. A clear image center alone does not establish surface height. Update a measurement only when identity correspondence and surface height are both resolved. During grasping, visible opposing outer edges or corners in the available calibrated views may constrain the center despite finger occlusion; otherwise carry the prior estimate. Do not infer a center from the desired waypoint or treat every small pixel shift as translation. For an elevated cover, estimate elevation only when resolvable known-size face geometry or available simultaneous calibrated views actually establish it. Otherwise carry the last reliably localized coordinate rather than projecting onto the resting plane or guessing an elevation correction. Update when reliable geometry becomes visible again. Replay the ordered tracking_frame list followed by the current clip chronologically, removing duplicate labels, to trace each specific container before measuring its endpoint. The list's first frame anchors correspondence; later frames preserve motion that may not permit metric localization. target_locations contains last reliable measurements, not guaranteed current positions. Separate identity tracking from metric localization: a stale coordinate must not force a new identity assignment, and retained frames do not by themselves resolve genuinely ambiguous correspondence. At crossings, use continuous motion through intermediate frames, allowing horizontal and vertical image ranking to change; do not transfer identity by nearest previous position, initial slot, or final spatial order alone. Compare successive front frames for residual translation, including during unrelated button motions: reaching a hand waypoint does not imply that covers have settled. First incorporate successful pickups observed this cycle into pickups_completed. Freeze entries at indices below that updated count at their incoming values; do not revise them during subsequent lift, lowering, or withdrawal observations. Update remaining entries after reliably localized translation, including movement during grasping. Preserve coordinates when images support stationarity rather than introducing estimation jitter. When localization is unreliable or temporarily occluded, carry the last reliable location without assuming the cover is stationary. Keep tracking later requested targets during button pressing and earlier pickups; use a newly exposed cube to confirm correspondence. Write coordinates to millimetre resolution without implying millimetre measurement accuracy. e.g. [[0.02, -0.18], [0.03, 0.13]]

For an elevated container, use an elevation estimate only when the images available through this cycle resolve it, for example from resolvable known-size face geometry or simultaneous calibrated views. Follow each container continuously through every shuffle, allowing its horizontal and vertical image ranking to change at crossings; neither its initial slot nor nearest position alone establishes identity. Audit correspondence through successive frames and correct erroneous annotations from their first occurrence, but assign each cycle only what its incoming memory and images available through that cycle establish. Later images must not resolve an earlier ambiguous crossing retrospectively. fields.name: interaction_state
fields.description: Initialize start. Update from observed outcomes and the incoming milestone, not from the action you are about to choose. A completed approach above the robot-left button gives left_hover; its subsequent short close-only motion gives left_ready; descent to button contact gives left_pressed; upward withdrawal gives left_retracted. Apply the analogous right_hover, right_ready, right_pressed, right_retracted milestones at the robot-right button. In particular, arrival with already-closed fingers is still right_hover, not right_ready: the separate short closing action must be observed. Opening after right_retracted gives buttons_finished. Arrival above the next requested container at about 0.20 m gives target_hover; descending and closing around it near 0.063 m gives target_grasped; lifting it clear near 0.20 m gives target_lifted; lowering and opening near 0.07 m gives target_released; withdrawing the empty hand near 0.15 m gives target_cleared. A subsequent approach to the next target returns to target_hover. Retain the incoming state if the expected outcome has not occurred or no control steps executed. e.g. "right_ready"
fields.annotation: Observed interaction milestone, initially start. Button milestones are left_hover, left_ready, left_pressed, left_retracted, right_hover, right_ready, right_pressed, right_retracted, buttons_finished. Hover means the initial approach to that button has finished; ready means the subsequent short closing action has finished, even if the fingers were already closed on arrival. Pressed means the closed hand has descended into button contact; retracted means it has subsequently risen to approximately 0.15 m. buttons_finished means the hand has subsequently opened above the right button. Container milestones are target_hover, target_grasped, target_lifted, target_released, target_cleared. They respectively mean arrival at the selected container's 0.20 m approach, closure around it near 0.063 m, successful lift near 0.20 m, lowering and opening near 0.07 m, and empty-hand withdrawal near 0.15 m. Change only when the corresponding motion outcome is observed, never when its waypoint is selected. e.g. "right_ready"

fields.name: pickups_completed
fields.description: Initialize zero. Increment only when the incoming state is target_grasped and the current clip shows the held requested container successfully raised clear to about 0.20 m, ordinarily revealing its colored cube. Carry the count unchanged in every other situation, including further views of that same held container. e.g. 1
fields.annotation: Number of requested containers successfully lifted in instruction order. Initialize to zero. Increment once when a newly grasped requested container is visibly raised off the table to approximately 0.20 m, exposing its cube. Do not increment for grasp closure, release, withdrawal, or repeated observations of the same lift. e.g. 1

texts.action:
Use the incoming memory together with outcomes visible this cycle to determine the current milestone; write those observations for the next cycle. Begin by locating both buttons and all requested colored cubes. Robot-left is larger world y, appearing on the right of the front image. Estimate geometry with the calibrated cameras, intersecting image rays with the appropriate object surface height rather than treating elevated tops as table points. Use wrist imagery to refine alignment. Do not reuse episode-specific coordinates.

Button rules: Independently localize each button using the center of its circular press surface, intersecting its calibrated image ray with approximately z=0.025 m. Do not use the square base centroid, a table-plane projection, the other button's x coordinate, or the achieved TCP position as its center. Prefer the current calibrated wrist view when the circle is visible. At hover and ready milestones, recompute the button center and command its x,y even if the preceding approach was accepted as complete or the closing action produced little motion. Hover tolerance establishes the milestone, not exact lateral alignment. All references below to the button center mean this visually localized center. From start, approach the robot-left button center at z=0.15 m, orientation [-3.1416,0,0], gripper open. At left_hover, command closure above the same center at z=0.15. At left_ready, descend over that center to commanded z=0.0075, closed. Actual contact may stop the TCP near z=0.024; this counts as contact, not a reason to press deeper. At left_pressed, retract over the localized left-button center to z=0.15 closed. At left_retracted, approach the robot-right button center at z=0.15 with an open command. At right_hover, perform the separate short closing action above the button even when the reported fingers are already closed. At right_ready, descend to z=0.0075 closed. At right_pressed, retract over the localized right-button center to z=0.15 closed. At right_retracted, open above the same button. Continue observing and tracking container exchanges throughout all these motions. Neither a return to the original spatial arrangement nor an unchanged shell appearance resets its hidden color association.

Container rules: Replay the retained tracking_frame list followed by the current clip chronologically to establish correspondence. target_locations stores last reliable measurements, not necessarily current positions. After buttons_finished or at target_cleared, select the requested target at index pickups_completed using its tracked identity, never the nearest cover to a stale coordinate. Before approaching or grasping, require unambiguous identity and reliable current localization. If ongoing motion or temporary occlusion prevents localization, use the existing purposeful settling wait or safe revealing withdrawal and reassess; do not assume waiting resolves a genuinely ambiguous completed exchange. Approach the resolved current center at z=0.20, open, pointing straight down. Choose yaw from its visible square edges so the fingers grasp opposing sides; use an equivalent square-symmetry orientation near zero where possible. At target_hover, descend to the container center at z=0.0633–0.0634 and close. At target_grasped, raise to z=0.20 closed, keeping the grasp orientation and approximately the container center's x,y; a small visual centering correction is appropriate. Fingers stopped around 0.018 m each and a container between them support a successful grasp.

At target_lifted, if more requested pickups remain, lower the held container using current TCP x,y to z=0.07 and open, preserving current orientation. Use current visible held-object geometry, not the frozen completed entry, to check placement. At target_released, withdraw vertically at current TCP x,y and orientation with open fingers to approximately z=0.149 before moving laterally to the next target. The completed pickup remains completed even though its cube is covered again. After lifting the final requested container, retain the grasp for automatic success; do not initiate an unnecessary release.

Never issue an exactly identical TCP pose merely to change the gripper. Apply this check only after correcting the nominal close/open waypoint's x,y from visual localization. If the corrected nominal waypoint is still within 2 mm of the current pose, add a small vertical displacement of about 3 mm while retaining the required gripper command. Do not add that offset when lateral correction already makes the waypoint nonidentical. Allow normal motion error when recognizing arrival; do not require exact equality.

If an expected motion did not execute, retain memory milestones and retry with a reachable, nonidentical waypoint. If alignment or grasp is visibly unsuccessful, correct using the current wrist image instead of advancing progress. If a target is temporarily occluded, first withdraw safely to reveal it. If containers are still moving and correspondence needs another observation, a short purposeful wait of 8 control steps may be used to finish tracking before a grasp. Do not guess a hidden color from its original slot, and do not wait without a specific visibility or settling purpose.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: At target_lifted, if more requested pickups remain, lower the held container using current TCP x,y to z=0.07 and open, preserving current orientation. Use current visible held-object geometry, not the frozen completed entry, to check placement. At target_released, withdraw vertically at current TCP x,y and orientation with open fingers to approximately z=0.149 before moving laterally to the next target.

Geometry-based localization, causal annotation, stationary-coordinate preservation, and continuous identity tracking remain in force.
